about: How Nuke's Properties-panel knob widgets behave, one entry per behaviour, from Foundry's Nuke 17.0 User Guide. Facts only: a behaviour the guide does not state is listed with status 'undocumented' and no claim. tools/nuke_panel_interactions.py drives NodeBased's real widgets against every documented entry (lane 10, 2026-11-16).

color.title: Using the Color Controls (Nuke 17.0 User Guide)

viewer_controls.title: Using the Viewer Controls (Nuke 17.0 User Guide)

tab_menu.title: Using the Tab Menu (Nuke 17.0 User Guide)

behaviours.nuke: Double-click the field to select the whole value and type a replacement.
behaviours.quote: Double-click in the field to select the whole value. Type the value you want to replace the selection.

behaviours.nuke: Arithmetic typed into a field is worked out on Enter: 378/2 gives 189.
behaviours.quote: if you wanted to halve a value of 378, you could simply type 378/2 into a field and press Enter to get 189.

behaviours.nuke: Typing = starts an expression in the field; the knob is then driven by that expression.
behaviours.quote: You always start an expression by typing =.

behaviours.nuke: With the cursor just before a digit, Up/Down change that digit by one unit (before the 0 of 20.51 steps by ones).
behaviours.quote: Click to insert the cursor just prior to the digit you want to increment or decrement. Press the up arrow to increment by one unit, or the down arrow to decrement by one unit.

behaviours.nuke: The mouse wheel increments and decrements the field.
behaviours.quote: You can also increment and decrement values by scrolling the mouse wheel

behaviours.nuke: Holding Alt while left-dragging on the value increments and decrements it.
behaviours.quote: or by holding Alt while left-mouse dragging on the value.

behaviours.nuke: Middle-mouse drag over a numeric field is a virtual slider; Shift increases and Alt decreases its sensitivity.
behaviours.quote: hover the cursor over a numeric control, click the middle-mouse button, and drag the field ... Hold Shift to increase slider sensitivity and Alt to decrease slider sensitivity.

behaviours.nuke: The regular slider beside the field edits the value (and keys it when the knob is animated).
behaviours.quote: Edit the parameter's value using the input field, regular slider, or color slider.

behaviours.nuke: The 17.0 User Guide does not say whether a typed value outside the slider's range is kept or clamped.
Clicking the colour swatch turns on the eye dropper; clicking it again closes it.
behaviours.quote: Click the color swatch to activate the eye dropper tool.

behaviours.nuke: With the eye dropper on, Ctrl/Cmd+click in the Viewer samples one pixel into the knob.
behaviours.quote: Ctrl/Cmd+click to sample a color value

behaviours.nuke: Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+drag samples a region; the knob takes the average colour of the region.
behaviours.quote: You can sample a region instead of just a single pixel by also pressing Shift+drag ... Nuke calculates the average color of the region.

behaviours.nuke: With the eye dropper on, Ctrl/Cmd+right-click in the Viewer discards the sampled pixels.
behaviours.quote: You can discard sampled pixels by Ctrl/Cmd+right-clicking in the Viewer.

behaviours.nuke: The colour picker button shows colour sliders and a wheel (in the panel or in a floating window).
behaviours.quote: The color picker button can be used to display and make color selections.

behaviours.nuke: The picker offers RGB(A), HSV and TMI slider sets.
behaviours.quote: From the TMI, HSV, and RGB buttons, you can select which slider you want to display.

behaviours.nuke: Dragging around the wheel sets hue, in and out sets saturation.
behaviours.quote: drag the marker on the edge of the wheel to adjust the hue, and drag the marker inside the wheel to adjust the saturation.

behaviours.nuke: Dragging one colour swatch onto another copies the colour.
behaviours.quote: You can copy a color from one swatch to another by dragging and dropping the color swatch

behaviours.nuke: Animation menu > Set key keys the current frame and the input field turns blue.
behaviours.quote: Select Set key from the dropdown menu. The parameter's input field turns blue, indicating that a keyframe has been inserted.

behaviours.nuke: Once a knob is keyed, changing its value on another frame sets a key there automatically.
behaviours.quote: Nuke switches to autokey mode: when you change the parameters value at another frame, it automatically inserts another keyframe for you.

behaviours.nuke: Animation menu > Delete key removes the key on the current frame.
behaviours.quote: Select Delete key from the dropdown menu. Nuke removes the keyframe.

behaviours.nuke: Animation menu > No animation removes every key and keeps the current frame's value as the static value.
behaviours.quote: Nuke removes all key frames from the parameter, and sets the static value to match that of the current frame.

behaviours.nuke: Right-clicking a node's properties panel offers Set key on all knobs.
behaviours.quote: right-click on a node's properties panel and select Set key on all knobs.

behaviours.nuke: Controls are linked through expressions entered from the Animation menu.
behaviours.quote: You can link any controls with others by using expressions

behaviours.nuke: The 17.0 User Guide pages read do not describe the Animation menu's Copy and Paste entries.
The 17.0 User Guide pages read do not describe a Set to default entry on the Animation menu.
The channel selector button shows how many channels the knob can be split into (four for R, G, B, A).
behaviours.quote: The number displayed on the channel selector button represents the number of available channels for editing.

behaviours.nuke: Clicking the channel selector shows one value field per channel; each can be typed separately.
behaviours.quote: Click the channel selector button. The available channels appear with value fields for each.

behaviours.nuke: Clicking the channel selector again closes the fields and keeps the per-channel values.
behaviours.quote: simply click the channel selector button again to close and save your settings.

behaviours.nuke: The guide does not say what the single field shows once differing channel values are closed.
The Node tab carries label, font, hide input, cached, disable, dope sheet, bookmark, postage stamp, static frame and lifetime range.
behaviours.quote: On the Node tab, you can usually adjust the following controls: label ... font ... hide input ... cached ... disable ... dope sheet ... bookmark ... postage stamp ... static frame ... lifeteme range

behaviours.nuke: The Node tab lists label, font (with bold, italic, size and text colour), hide input, cached, disable, dope sheet, bookmark, postage stamp, static frame and lifetime range, in that order.
behaviours.quote: label ... font ... Bolds any text ... Emphasizes any text ... font size ... color of any text ... hide input ... cached ... disable ... dope sheet ... bookmark ... postage stamp ... static frame ... lifeteme range

behaviours.nuke: The disable box disables the node; unchecking re-enables it.
behaviours.quote: Check this to disable the node. Uncheck to re-enable.

behaviours.nuke: The guide pages read show dropdown menus but state no interaction rule beyond choosing an entry.
No rule beyond checking and unchecking is stated for ordinary check boxes.
Choosing a layer in a node's channels field shows that layer's channels with check boxes; unchecked channels are not processed.
behaviours.quote: From the channels field, select the layer containing the channels you wish to process. The layer's channels appear with check boxes. Deselect those channels which you don't wish to process.

behaviours.nuke: To process one channel, set the channels field to none and pick the channel in the right-most channel field.
behaviours.quote: From the channels field, select none. From the right most channel field - the one which typically calls the alpha channel - select the single channel you wish to process.

behaviours.nuke: XY knob interaction (two fields plus a Viewer handle) is not described on the User Guide pages read.
File knob browsing is described on the Read node pages, not the knob pages read here.
A node with mask controls offers a mask channel menu, an inject box, an invert box and a mix slider.
behaviours.quote: select the channel you want to use from the mask dropdown menu ... check inject ... check the invert box to reverse the mask ... adjusting the mix slider.

behaviours.nuke: The User Guide pages read do not describe the fringe box's interaction; its effect is on the node reference pages.
Inserting a node shows its panel in the Properties bin.
behaviours.quote: When you insert a node, its properties automatically appear in the Properties panel

behaviours.nuke: Double-clicking a node in the Node Graph opens its panel.
behaviours.quote: Double-click on the node in the Node Graph.

behaviours.nuke: Ctrl/Cmd+click on a node in the Node Graph opens its panel.
behaviours.quote: Ctrl/Cmd+click on the node in the Node Graph.

behaviours.nuke: With a node selected in the Node Graph, Return opens its panel.
behaviours.quote: Select the node in the Node Graph and press Return.

behaviours.nuke: Ctrl/Cmd+double-click (or Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+click) opens the panel in a floating window.
behaviours.quote: To open a properties panel in a floating window, Ctrl/Cmd+double-click or Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+click on the node.

behaviours.nuke: A field on the Properties panel sets the most node panels it holds open.
behaviours.quote: You can limit the number of node panels that can be open in the Properties panel. To do so, enter the maximum number of nodes in the field on the Properties panel.

behaviours.nuke: The lock button keeps the bin as it is and sends every new panel to a floating window.
behaviours.quote: To lock the Properties panel and have all new panels appear in floating windows, click the lock button on the Properties panel.

behaviours.nuke: The remove all panels button empties the bin.
behaviours.quote: To empty the Properties panel and close all the node panels in it, click the remove all panels button.

behaviours.nuke: A panel's close (X) button closes that panel.
behaviours.quote: Closes the node panel.

behaviours.nuke: Alt+click on a panel's close button closes every panel in the bin.
behaviours.quote: You can also close all the nodes in the Properties panel by Alt+clicking on the close (X) button of one of the nodes.

behaviours.nuke: Ctrl/Cmd+click on a panel's close button closes every other panel.
behaviours.quote: Ctrl/Cmd+click to close all panels except the one clicked on.

behaviours.nuke: A panel's float button floats it; clicking it again docks it back.
behaviours.quote: Floats the panel. Clicking this button again docks the panel back into the pane if the originating pane is open.

behaviours.nuke: A panel's header button hides or shows its tabbed pages (the panel minimises to its header).
behaviours.quote: Hide or show the node’s tabbed pages.

behaviours.nuke: The pages read do not say where in the bin a newly opened panel goes (NodeBased puts it on top).
The pages read give no default for the maximum-panels field or say which panel closes when it is exceeded (NodeBased closes the oldest).
The pages read describe locking the whole bin, not pinning one panel; NodeBased keeps every opened panel until it is closed or pushed out by the limit.
Right-click a knob > Add expression, or type = in it, opens the expression dialog.
behaviours.quote: right-click on the parameter and select Add expression, OR type = in the parameter field.

behaviours.nuke: An expression naming another node's knob (Node.knob) makes this knob take that knob's value.
behaviours.quote: Through expressions, you can link the parameters from one node and control the values of the parameters in other nodes.

behaviours.nuke: Ctrl/Cmd+dragging one knob onto another links the second to the first with an expression.
behaviours.quote: Ctrl/Cmd+drag the parameter that has the values you want to use on top of the parameter that receives these values. This links the parameters

behaviours.nuke: A linked knob turns blue.
behaviours.quote: This links the parameters, which turn blue.

behaviours.nuke: The Node Graph draws a green arrow between nodes linked by an expression.
behaviours.quote: In the Node Graph, a green arrow appears between the nodes to indicate that they are linked via an expression.

behaviours.nuke: Right-click the linked knob > Edit expression (or press = on it) to see or change the link.
behaviours.quote: To edit the expression later on, right-click on the parameter and select Edit expression (or press = on the parameter).

behaviours.nuke: Ctrl/Cmd+dragging one knob's animation button onto another's links all the values beside them at once.
behaviours.quote: If you want to link several parameters at the same time, Ctrl/Cmd+drag the animation button next to the source parameters on top of the animation button next to the destination parameters.

behaviours.nuke: Channel, layer and format knobs carry a Link menu: Set link, Edit link, Remove link, and Ctrl/Cmd+drag of the menu onto another control.
behaviours.quote: You can link controls using the Link menu next to the control on the properties panel

behaviours.nuke: The Animation menu's Link to > Tracker linking dialog links a knob to a Tracker's track.
behaviours.quote: Select Link to > Tracker linking dialog...

behaviours.nuke: The pages read do not say how to remove an expression link from a number knob (No animation is described for keys only). NodeBased's knob menu has Clear expression.
The pages read do not describe copying and pasting a knob's value or animation from the Properties panel (the Curve Editor's Copy Links is a Curve Editor command).
Reading another frame (Node.knob(10), (t-2)) is part of the expression language, outside the panel interactions measured here.
Tab opens a list of matches as you type; Up/Down and Return creates the chosen node after the selected one.
behaviours.quote: Press the Tab key and start typing the name of the node you want to create. This opens a prompt displaying a list of matches.

behaviours.nuke: Tab then Return adds the last node created from the Tab menu.
behaviours.quote: To add the last node created using this method, simply press Tab and then Return.

behaviours.nuke: Nodes used often from the Tab menu are listed higher; keyboard shortcuts do not count.
behaviours.quote: Commonly added nodes carry more weight and are listed higher up in the node list.

behaviours.nuke: A new node is connected to the selected node.
behaviours.quote: When you add a node, Nuke automatically connects it to the currently selected node.

behaviours.nuke: Shift while creating adds the node in a new branch after the selected one.
behaviours.quote: Hold down Shift and create the node using the Toolbar, Tab menu, or right-click menu.

behaviours.nuke: Ctrl/Cmd while creating replaces the selected node.
behaviours.quote: To replace a node in Nuke, simply hold down Ctrl/Cmd and create a new node.

behaviours.nuke: Dragging a node onto the pipe between two connected nodes inserts it between them.
behaviours.quote: drag the node into the space between the already connected nodes ... it is automatically placed and connected between the two nodes.

behaviours.nuke: Dragging a pipe's head or tail to empty space disconnects it.
behaviours.quote: You can disconnect nodes by either dragging the head or tail of the connecting arrow to an empty area of the workspace

behaviours.nuke: Ctrl/Cmd+D disconnects the selected node.
behaviours.quote: or selecting the lower node in the tree and pressing Ctrl/Cmd+D.

behaviours.nuke: Dropping a pipe's end on a node connects it there.
behaviours.quote: You can reconnect a node by dragging the head or tail of the connecting arrow and drop it over the center of the node

behaviours.nuke: Shift+dragging a pipe onto a node duplicates the connection and keeps the original.
behaviours.quote: To duplicate a connecting arrow, hold Shift and drag the connecting arrow on top of the node you want to create a connection to.

behaviours.nuke: Ctrl/Cmd+clicking the dot on a pipe adds a Dot there.
behaviours.quote: You can also add a dot to an existing connection by pressing Ctrl/Cmd and clicking on the yellow dot that appears on the connecting arrow.

behaviours.nuke: Shift+click adds a node to the selection.
behaviours.quote: press Shift while clicking on each node you want to select

behaviours.nuke: Ctrl/Cmd while dragging a node selects every node upstream of it.
behaviours.quote: Press Ctrl/Cmd while dragging a node. Nuke selects all nodes that feed data to the selected node.

behaviours.nuke: Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+A selects every node connected to the selected one, upstream and downstream.
behaviours.quote: select Edit > Select Connected Nodes (or press Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+A).

behaviours.nuke: Ctrl/Cmd+A selects every node.
behaviours.quote: Select Edit > Select all (or press Ctrl/Cmd+A).

behaviours.nuke: D disables or re-enables the selected nodes.
behaviours.quote: Select Edit > Node > Disable/Enable (or press D).

behaviours.nuke: Ctrl/Cmd+C copies; Ctrl/Cmd+V pastes, connected to the node selected before pasting.
behaviours.quote: When you paste nodes, Nuke automatically connects them to the node that is selected before the paste operation.

behaviours.nuke: Ctrl/Cmd+X cuts the selected nodes.
behaviours.quote: Choose Edit > Cut (or press Ctrl/Cmd+X).

behaviours.nuke: Edit > Clone makes a copy that keeps an active link to its parent, drawn with an orange line.
behaviours.quote: Nuke clones the node(s), while maintaining an active link to the parental node(s).

behaviours.nuke: N opens a rename field on top of the selected node.
behaviours.quote: Press N. Enter a new name for the node in the rename field that appears on top of the node.

behaviours.nuke: Nodes are coloured by their class (Preferences > Node Colors > autocolor).
behaviours.quote: autocolor ... Use this to select the color to use as default for all nodes not otherwise specified above

behaviours.nuke: The Node tab's colour changes the node's colour in the Node Graph.
behaviours.quote: You can modify the color, name, and notes that a particular node displays.

behaviours.nuke: Moving a Backdrop moves every node that overlaps it.
behaviours.quote: When you move the box, all the nodes that overlap the box are moved too.

behaviours.nuke: With snap to grid on, dragged nodes snap to the grid.
behaviours.quote: When enabled, nodes snap into positions (while dragging them) that line them up with the grid.

behaviours.nuke: The pages read do not describe swapping two inputs with Shift (Nuke's Shift+X swap is not on them).
The pages read describe upstream selection (Ctrl/Cmd+drag) and Select Connected, not a downstream-only selection.
The pages read name Edit > Clone and Copy as Clones (Ctrl+K), not an Alt+C duplicate; NodeBased's Alt+C copies and pastes in one step.
Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+click adds a key, on the curve or off it.
behaviours.quote: Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+click on the part of the Curve Editor you want to add a point to. You can add points both on the curve and outside the curve

behaviours.nuke: A plain drag moves a key along x or y only.
behaviours.quote: To move a point along either the x or y axis only, drag the point to a new location.

behaviours.nuke: Ctrl/Cmd+drag moves a key in any direction.
behaviours.quote: To move a point in any direction, Ctrl+drag (Mac users Cmd+drag) the point to a new location.

behaviours.nuke: A moved key's x is rounded to the nearest whole frame; Shift turns that off while moving.
behaviours.quote: By default, when you move a point, its position on the x axis is rounded to the nearest integer.

behaviours.nuke: A selected key's x and y can be typed in.
behaviours.quote: To adjust the values of a point numerically, select the point and double-click on the x or y value that appears next to it.

behaviours.nuke: A selected key shows tangent handles; dragging one bends the curve.
behaviours.quote: Select a point on the curve. Red tangent handles appear on both sides of the point. Drag the tangent handles to a new location. The curve follows the handles.

behaviours.nuke: Right-click > Interpolation lists Constant, Linear, Smooth, Catmull-Rom, Cubic, Horizontal and Break.
behaviours.quote: Right-click on the Editor. Select Interpolation and the type of interpolation you want to use.

behaviours.nuke: Constant holds the value after the key; Linear draws straight lines between keys.
behaviours.quote: Constant to force a constant value after each selected point. Linear to use linear interpolation. This produces sharp changes at key frames and straight lines between them.

behaviours.nuke: Smooth takes the neighbours' slope, but is flat at a key above or below both neighbours, so the curve never overshoots.
behaviours.quote: If the selected point is not between these key frames and has a larger or smaller value than both key frames, the tangents' slopes are made horizontal.

behaviours.nuke: Catmull-Rom takes the neighbours' slope regardless; Cubic makes the second derivative continuous.
behaviours.quote: Catmull-Rom to set the tangents' slope equal to the slope between the keyframe to the left and the keyframe to the right regardless of where the selected point is located. Cubic to set the slope so that the second derivative is continuous.

behaviours.nuke: Horizontal sets the key's slope to zero.
behaviours.quote: Horizontal to make the tangents horizontal, setting the slope around the selected points to zero.

behaviours.nuke: Break lets the key's two tangents move independently.
behaviours.quote: Break to adjust the two tangents of a selected point independent of each other.

behaviours.nuke: The mouse wheel and the + and - keys zoom.
behaviours.quote: Press the + button to zoom in, or the - button to zoom out, OR Scroll up with the mouse wheel to zoom in, or down to zoom out.

behaviours.nuke: Middle-drag or Alt+drag pans.
behaviours.quote: To pan in the Editor, hold the middle-mouse button and drag over the Editor. You can also use Alt+drag.

behaviours.nuke: A (View > Frame All) resets zoom and pan.
behaviours.quote: From the menu that opens, select View > Frame All. OR Press A on the Editor.

behaviours.nuke: F (View > Frame Selected) centres the selected keys.
behaviours.quote: Right-click on the Editor, and select View > Frame Selected (or press F on the Editor).

behaviours.nuke: Shift+click or a marquee selects several keys, and the selection drags as one.
behaviours.quote: To select multiple points, Shift+click on the points, or drag a marquee around them.

behaviours.nuke: Ctrl/Cmd+A selects every key.
behaviours.quote: To select all points, press Ctrl+A (Mac users press Cmd+A).

behaviours.nuke: Several knobs' curves can be shown at once by Shift or Ctrl/Cmd+clicking in the parameter tree.
behaviours.quote: To focus on multiple curves at the same time, either: Hold Shift and click on curves to create a consecutive list, OR Hold Ctrl/Cmd and click on individual curves to add them to the selection.

behaviours.nuke: Edit > Move opens Move Animation Keys, which shifts the selected keys by a typed x and y (for example x+10).
behaviours.quote: Right-click on the editor and select Edit > Move. The Move Animation Keys dialog opens.

behaviours.nuke: An expression field at the bottom of the Curve Editor sets the curve, with Revert.
behaviours.quote: Enter the expression in the expression field at the bottom of the Curve Editor

behaviours.nuke: The Curve Editor section does not name a way to delete a key; NodeBased deletes the selected key with Delete/Backspace or the right-click menu.
The pages do not say how edits undo; NodeBased takes one undo step per key added, moved, deleted or retyped.
Each node with keys has a row, and each keyframe a marker on its frame.
behaviours.quote: Your keyframes display as gray markers in the keyframe grid.

behaviours.nuke: The current frame shows as a vertical line.
behaviours.quote: The current frame indicator displays as an orange line.

behaviours.nuke: The project's first and last frames show as their own lines.
behaviours.quote: The first and last frame in the project's frame range (as defined in the Project Settings) display as white/gray lines.

behaviours.nuke: Clicking a key selects it and shows its frame number beside it.
behaviours.quote: Click it in the keyframe view. Its parent keyframe and all other keyframes depending on it are selected too. The frame number of the keyframe is displayed next to it.

behaviours.nuke: Dragging a marquee over keys selects them; Shift adds or removes.
behaviours.quote: Drag a marquee over your keyframes in the keyframe view.

behaviours.nuke: Clicking a node's name selects all its keys.
behaviours.quote: Click the node name in the hierarchy view. All the child keyframes under that node are selected.

behaviours.nuke: Delete/Backspace erases the selected keys.
behaviours.quote: To delete a keyframe, just select it and press Delete/Backspace button or right-click on the keyframe and select Edit > Erase.

behaviours.nuke: Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+click on an empty spot adds a key.
behaviours.quote: Add keyframes by Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+clicking on an empty spot in the Dope sheet.

behaviours.nuke: Moved keys cannot pass other keys.
behaviours.quote: You cannot move keyframes past other keyframes.

behaviours.nuke: A Move field at the bottom moves the selected keys by a typed number of frames.
behaviours.quote: Move the selected keyframes by the number of frames specified. You can enter negative values to move the keyframes backwards.

behaviours.nuke: Ctrl/Cmd+C and Ctrl/Cmd+V copy keys and paste them relative to the current frame.
behaviours.quote: When using the Ctrl/Cmd+V keyboard shortcut, pasting keyframes is relative to the location of the current frame indicator.

behaviours.nuke: Reads with open panels show as gray bars that drag to reposition the clip.
behaviours.quote: Any Read nodes that have their properties panels open display as gray bars in the Dope Sheet.

behaviours.nuke: The page names the Move field but does not describe dragging keys; NodeBased drags the selected keys in time as one undo step, never past another key.
The pages read do not describe scaling keys in time in the Dope Sheet.
The pages do not describe the frame numbers along the top; NodeBased draws a ruler and a click there moves the playhead.
R, G, B and A show the red, green, blue and alpha channel.
behaviours.quote: You can press the R , G , B , and A keys on your keyboard to display the red, green, blue, and alpha channels respectively.

behaviours.nuke: Pressing the same channel key again returns to all channels.
behaviours.quote: Press one of the channel keys again to toggle back and display all channels.

behaviours.nuke: M shows the alpha as a red overlay on the RGB; M again returns.
behaviours.quote: Press M . Nuke displays the image’s alpha channel as a red overlay on top of the RGB channels.

behaviours.nuke: A number key shows the Viewer input with that number.
behaviours.quote: To view a particular node press the number key ( 1, 2, 3... 0 ) corresponding to the pipe number whose contents you wish to view.

behaviours.nuke: Up and Down cycle through the Viewer's wired inputs.
behaviours.quote: If a Viewer node has multiple inputs, like the one depicted above, you can press the up or down arrow keys to quickly cycle through the views

behaviours.nuke: Middle-drag, or Alt+drag, pans; the frame follows the pointer.
behaviours.quote: To pan the frame, hold the middle-mouse button and drag on the display (you can also use Alt +drag). The frame follows the mouse pointer.

behaviours.nuke: F re-centres the frame.
behaviours.quote: You can re-center the frame by clicking the middle-mouse button or pressing F .

behaviours.nuke: A middle-button click re-centres the frame.
behaviours.quote: You can re-center the frame by clicking the middle-mouse button or pressing F .

behaviours.nuke: + zooms in and - zooms out, repeatedly.
behaviours.quote: Press the plus button ( + ) repeatedly until the frame attains the desired scale.

behaviours.nuke: Dragging with the middle and left buttons held zooms about the pointer.
behaviours.quote: Drag the mouse while pressing the middle mouse button and the left mouse button.

behaviours.nuke: Ctrl/Cmd+1 restores the zoom to 100%.
behaviours.quote: You can restore the zoom to 100% by pressing Ctrl / Cmd + 1 .

behaviours.nuke: Alt+Z keeps the zoom when switching between inputs of different sizes.
behaviours.quote: Alternatively, you can also press Alt+Z on Viewer, or toggle prevent auto zoom in the Viewer settings.

behaviours.nuke: { hides or shows the top toolbar and } the bottom one.
behaviours.quote: To hide or show the top toolbar, press { . To hide or show the bottom toolbar, press } .

behaviours.nuke: The info bar shows the format, the bounding box and the pixel under the pointer: x, y and its RGBA.
behaviours.quote: the pixel's x and y position and its Red, Green, Blue, and Alpha values

behaviours.nuke: Ctrl/Cmd+click samples one pixel into the info bar.
behaviours.quote: You can sample a single pixel from the Viewer by pressing Ctrl/Cmd while clicking

behaviours.nuke: Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+drag samples a region.
behaviours.quote: a region from the Viewer by pressing Ctrl/Cmd + Shift while dragging

behaviours.nuke: Ctrl/Cmd+right-click cancels a sample.
behaviours.quote: To cancel a pixel selection, hold Ctrl / Cmd and right-click in the Viewer.

behaviours.nuke: The gain and gamma toggle buttons switch between 1 and the last value set.
behaviours.quote: The gain, gamma and saturation toggle buttons let you switch between the default values of 1 (no change) and the last gain and gamma adjustments you made in the Viewer.

behaviours.nuke: U refreshes the Viewer by hand.
behaviours.quote: You can click the 'Refresh Viewer' button (or press U ) to manually update the display

behaviours.nuke: Alt+G opens a Go to frame dialog.
behaviours.quote: choosing Viewer > Go to frame (or by pressing Alt + G ), entering a frame number in the dialog that appears, and clicking OK .

behaviours.nuke: The current frame field accepts +/-20 to jump by 20 frames.
behaviours.quote: The current frame and in an out point fields also accept simple mathematical functions, such as +/-20 to jump forward or backward 20 frames.

behaviours.nuke: The Viewer pages read do not describe a Y (luminance) key; NodeBased has none.
The Viewer pages describe the mouse wheel only for the timeline; NodeBased's wheel zooms the picture about the pointer.
The Viewer pages describe the play buttons but no J, K, L keys; NodeBased keeps J (back), K (stop), L (forward).
The Viewer pages read do not describe the A/B wipe or its handle; NodeBased keeps Alt+number for B and Shift+W to reset the wipe.
The Viewer pages read do not describe the proxy or region-of-interest toggles; NodeBased keeps Ctrl+P for proxy.
